chunks: The sick person performs salat standing. If he is unable to do that, he performs salat sitting. If he is unable to perform salat sitting, he performs salat lying on his back. He says the takbir, then recites. When he wants to perform ruku', he closes his eyes, then recites tasbih. When he has recited tasbih, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes serves as the raising of his head from ruku'. When he wants to perform sajdah, he closes his eyes, then recites tasbih. When he has recited tasbih, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes serves as the raising of his head from sajdah. Then he recites the tashahhud and departs.

key_terms.الْمَرِيضُ: the sick person who is the subject of this legal ruling
key_terms.جَالِسًا: sitting, the alternate posture when standing is not possible
key_terms.قَائِمًا: standing, the original posture for performing salat
key_terms.مُسْتَلْقِيًا: lying on the back, the posture used when even sitting is not possible
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدُ: he recites the tashahhud at the end of the prayer

ai.seo_question: How should a sick person perform salat if they cannot stand, sit, or make full bowing and prostration?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for how a sick person performs salat according to his ability, moving from standing to sitting to lying down when necessary. It also describes symbolic motions for ruku' and sajdah when physical movement is not possible, showing the flexibility of worship in cases of illness.
